nodes.summary: Nonzero solutions of a two-equation system modulo primes greater than 3 congruent to 3 mod 4. Let $n > 3$ be a prime with $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. Then there are nonzero $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ and an integer $r \in \{2, 3\}$ such that $x + ry = 0$ and $xy^r = 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Nonzero solutions of a two-equation system modulo primes greater than 3 congruent to 3 mod 4

nodes.summary: Let $F_1$ be the family over $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to $\sum_i b_i + \prod_i b_i$. Then $F_1$ is $1$-vanishing: every sequence over $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$ contains a block of consecutive terms, of some length $l > 1$, on which $F_1$ vanishes.
nodes.title: The sum-plus-product family is $1$-vanishing over $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every family $F$ of functions $f^{(l)} : (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^l \to M$, $l \ge 0$, into a type $M$ with a zero element, $F$ is $0$-vanishing.
nodes.title: Every family is $0$-vanishing

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F = (f^{(l)})_{l \ge 0}$ be a family of functions $f^{(l)} : (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^l \to M$ into a type $M$ with a zero element. For a natural number $m$, $F$ is $m$-vanishing if for every sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ of elements of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ there are a length $l > 1$ and a start $s \ge 0$ such that $f^{(l)}(a_{s+jl}, a_{s+jl+1}, \dots, a_{s+jl+l-1}) = 0$…
nodes.title: $m$-vanishing family

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $k > 0$ and $n = p^k$, and let $F_{-1}$ be the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to $\sum_i b_i - \prod_i b_i$. Then $F_{-1}$ is vanishing.
nodes.title: The sum-minus-product family is vanishing modulo prime powers

nodes.summary: The sum-plus-product family is vanishing over $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/8\mathbb{Z}$. Let $n \in \{4, 8\}$ and let $F_1$ be the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to $\sum_i b_i + \prod_i b_i$. Then $F_1$ is vanishing.
nodes.title: The sum-plus-product family is vanishing over $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/8\mathbb{Z}$

nodes.summary: Let $F_1$ be the family over $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to $\sum_i b_i + \prod_i b_i$. Then $F_1$ is vanishing.
nodes.title: The sum-plus-product family is vanishing over $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to $\sum_i b_i$ is vanishing: for every $m > 0$, every sequence over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ contains $m$ consecutive blocks of a common length $l > 1$, each with sum zero.
nodes.title: Zero-sum van der Waerden theorem

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer, $d$ a natural number and $g_1, \dots, g_d : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ maps. Then the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sending a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ to the vector $\left(\sum_i g_1(b_i), \dots, \sum_i g_d(b_i)\right) \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^d$ is vanishing, where a block counts as vanishing when all $d$ coordinates of this vector are zero.
nodes.title: Vanishing of families of sums of transformed entries

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A family $F$ of functions on blocks over $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with values in a type with a zero is vanishing if it is $m$-vanishing for every positive integer $m$.
nodes.title: Vanishing family

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a family of functions on blocks over $\mathbb{Z}/n$ with values in a type $M$ with a zero. If $F$ is $m$-vanishing and $m' \le m$, then $F$ is $m'$-vanishing.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of $m$-vanishing

nodes.summary: For every $m > 1$, neither of the sum-plus-product families $F_{-1}$ and $F_1$ over $\mathbb{Z}/6$, where $F_c(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + c\, b_1 \cdots b_l$, is $m$-vanishing.
nodes.title: $F_{\pm 1}$ over $\mathbb{Z}/6$ is not $m$-vanishing for $m > 1$

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a prime with $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. Then for every $m > 0$ the sum-plus-product family $F_1$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$, $F_1(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + b_1 \cdots b_l$, is not $m$-vanishing.
nodes.title: $F_1$ modulo a prime $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ is not $m$-vanishing for $m > 0$

nodes.summary: Let $n > 3$ be a prime with $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. Then for every $m > 0$ the sum-plus-product family $F_1$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$, $F_1(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + b_1 \cdots b_l$, is not $m$-vanishing.
nodes.title: $F_1$ modulo a prime $n > 3$ with $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ is not $m$-vanishing for $m > 0$

nodes.summary: Let $u > 1$ be a natural number and $n = 8u$. Then for every $m > 0$ the sum-plus-product family $F_1$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$, $F_1(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + b_1 \cdots b_l$, is not $m$-vanishing.
nodes.title: $F_1$ modulo $8u$ with $u > 1$ is not $m$-vanishing for $m > 0$

nodes.summary: Let $u > 0$ be a natural number and $n = 9u$. Then for every $m > 0$ the sum-plus-product family $F_1$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$, $F_1(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + b_1 \cdots b_l$, is not $m$-vanishing.
nodes.title: $F_1$ modulo $9u$ with $u > 0$ is not $m$-vanishing for $m > 0$

nodes.summary:
Let $n > 1$ and let $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n$ with $c 
e 0$, $c 
e 1$ and $c 
e -1$. Then for every $m > 0$ the sum-plus-product family $F_c$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$, $F_c(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + c\, b_1 \cdots b_l$, is not $m$-vanishing.
nodes.title: $F_c$ with $c \notin \{0, \pm 1\}$ is not $m$-vanishing for $m > 0$

nodes.summary: For $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n$ and $b_0, b_1 \in \mathbb{Z}/n$, the sum-plus-product family $F_c$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$ satisfies $F_c(b_0, b_1) = b_0 + b_1 + c\, b_0 b_1$.
nodes.title: The sum-plus-product family on blocks of length two

nodes.summary: For $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n$, the family $F_c$ over $\mathbb{Z}/n$ sends a block $(b_1, \dots, b_l)$ of elements of $\mathbb{Z}/n$, of any length $l \ge 0$, to $b_1 + \dots + b_l + c\, b_1 b_2 \cdots b_l$, where an empty sum is $0$ and an empty product is $1$.
nodes.title: The sum-plus-product family $F_c$

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ and let $F_1$ be the family over $\mathbb{Z}/n$ given by $F_1(b_1, \dots, b_l) = b_1 + \dots + b_l + b_1 \cdots b_l$. If $n \notin \{2, 3, 4, 6, 8\}$, then $F_1$ is not $m$-vanishing for any $m > 0$. If $n \in \{2, 3, 4, 8\}$, then $F_1$ is vanishing. If $n = 6$, then $F_1$ is $1$-vanishing but not $m$-vanishing for any $m > 1$.
nodes.title: Classification of vanishing for the sum-plus-product family $F_1$
